title: On Saving the boy from the second wave
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：save　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 save 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the postman ① saved the boy from the second wave without complaint, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② saves the boy from the second wave with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ save the boy from the second wave at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ saved the boy from the second wave before — a line in the list for June 1973 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Saving the boy from the second wave without complaint, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ save two pounds every month with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Save two pounds every month at once and never mention it again.

By 1986 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ saves two pounds every month without complaint every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ saved the boy from the second wave again when nobody else would.

⑩ To save the boy from the second wave, my mother said in 1991, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody saves the boy from the second wave with great care again and somebody must save the boy from the second wave without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 挽救（一般过去式 saved the boy from the second wave：1979 年邮差头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 挽救（一般现在 saves the boy from the second wave：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 挽救（不定式 to save the boy from the second wave：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 挽救（过去完成时 had saved the boy from the second wave：1973 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 挽救（动名词 saving the boy from the second wave 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 节省（save two pounds every month：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去节省每月省下两镑）
G. v. 节省（save two pounds every month：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 挽救（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 saves two pounds every month，而母亲又一次 saved the boy from the second wave）

answers.why: save 意为“挽救”，1979 年邮差毫无怨言地挽救把那孩子从第二道浪里救出，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 saved。
save 意为“挽救”，自那以后邮差小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 saves。
save 意为“挽救”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯挽救把那孩子从第二道浪里救出”，此处为不定式 to save the boy from the second wave。
save 意为“挽救”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1986 年之前就有人挽救过，故用过去完成时 had saved。
save 意为“挽救”，邮差说“挽救把那孩子从第二道浪里救出这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 saving the boy from the second wave 作主语。
save 意为“节省”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去节省每月省下两镑”，should ever 之后用原形 save two pounds every month。
save 意为“节省”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻节省每月省下两镑（save two pounds every month at once），以后再也不要提起。
save 意为“挽救”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例节省每月省下两镑，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 saves。
save 意为“挽救”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地挽救把那孩子从第二道浪里救出，用一般过去式 saved 叙述。
save 意为“挽救”，结尾那句是母亲 1991 年的话：要挽救把那孩子从第二道浪里救出，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 save 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1979 the postman saved the boy from the second wave without complaint, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman saves the boy from the second wave with great care whenever the office asks.
Saving the boy from the second wave without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever save two pounds every month with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office saves two pounds every month without complaint every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother saved the boy from the second wave again, and the office remembered that half.
